error.ageRecipient: That doesn't look like an age recipient. It starts with age1.
error.code: Type the 6 digits from your authenticator app.
error.credentials: The email or password is wrong, or the code has expired.
error.email: Type an email address, like name@example.co.
error.insecureContext: Setup needs HTTPS, or a browser on the server itself. Open this page at your reverse proxy's HTTPS address.
error.network: Can't reach the server. Check your connection and try again.
error.passwordShort: Use at least 12 characters. A few words in a row work well.
error.port: A port is a number from 1 to 65535.
error.rateLimited: Too many tries. Wait {seconds, plural, one {# second} other {# seconds}} and try again.
error.server: The server had a problem. Try again in a moment.
error.serverKeyStored: Confirm you've kept a copy of server.key.
error.setupCode: The setup code is 12 letters and digits, like 7QF4-9M2X-HD3P.
error.setupCodeWrong: That setup code is wrong. After a few wrong tries you wait a little longer before each new one.
error.setupComplete: Setup has already been done on this server.
error.stale: Another app changed this item first. It has been reloaded: look it over and save again.
error.twoStepRequired: Turn on a two-step method before finishing setup.
error.url: Type a web address that starts with https:// or http://.
state.error.title: This page didn't load
state.error.body: Something stopped the page from opening. Try again.
state.offline.title: Can't reach the server
state.offline.body: Check that Kemlock Server is running and that this address is right.
state.notFound.title: No such page
state.notFound.body: The address doesn't lead anywhere here.
setup.code.title: Welcome to Kemlock Server
setup.code.lede: This server is new and has no admin yet. To show you're the one who runs it, type the setup code it printed in its log when it first started.
setup.code.find: Where to find the setup code
setup.code.elsewhere: Where to look, by how you run the server
setup.code.whereBinary: The terminal the server runs in.
setup.code.whereUnraid: Docker tab, the kemlock icon, then Logs.
setup.code.whereHa: Settings, Add-ons, Kemlock Server, then the Log tab.
setup.code.whereSynology: Container Manager, Container, kemlock, then Log.
setup.code.whereQnap: Container Station, Applications, kemlock, then Log.
setup.code.dockerName: Put your container's name where the command says container. Run docker ps to find it.
setup.code.label: Setup code
setup.code.hint: Wrong tries slow it down: after a few, you wait a little longer before each new one.
setup.code.note1: The code makes the first admin, and nothing else. It stops working the moment that account exists.
setup.code.note2: Lose the admin account later? Run kemlock-cli reset-admin on the server.
setup.code.insecure: This address isn't HTTPS or localhost. The keys this browser makes need a secure connection, and the server refuses setup without one. Open this page at your reverse proxy's HTTPS address.
setup.admin.title: Make the first admin
setup.admin.lede: The code worked. This is an ordinary Kemlock account with the admin role, so it holds your own vault too. Admin actions ask you to confirm with your passkey or password again.
setup.admin.name: Name
setup.admin.passwordHint: Nobody can reset it for you, not even this server. A Recovery Kit, offered at the end, is your way back.
setup.admin.passkeyHint: Your browser asks for it on the next step. If its authenticator supports PRF it also opens your vault; if not, the master password does.
setup.admin.strength.0: Too simple. Add more words or characters.
setup.admin.strength.1: Weak. Add more words or characters.
setup.admin.strength.2: Fair. A few more characters would help.
setup.admin.strength.3: Good. One more word would make it strong.
setup.admin.keys.title: Your keys are made here, in this browser
setup.admin.keys.body: The master password never leaves it. Sign-in uses OPAQUE, so the server never sees the password or a hash of it.
setup.admin.keys.user: A user key. Wrapped twice: under your Argon2id master key, and under OPAQUE's export key.
setup.twoStep.title: Turn on two-step login
setup.twoStep.lede: Admin accounts sign in with a second step after the master password. Pick one now; you can add the other later in Account security.
setup.twoStep.appHint: A 6-digit code that changes every 30 seconds
setup.twoStep.keyHint: Touch a USB or NFC key, or use a passkey
setup.twoStep.keyPrompt: Your browser asks you to touch the key or approve the passkey. Keep it somewhere safe: it is the second step each time you sign in.
setup.twoStep.passkeyFailed: Your authenticator app is on, but the passkey was not made. Add it later in Account security.
setup.twoStep.passkeyFailedKey: Your security key is on, but the passkey was not made. Add it later in Account security.
setup.twoStep.scanTitle: Add this server to your authenticator app
setup.twoStep.qr: QR code that adds {host}, {email}, to an authenticator app
setup.twoStep.scan: Scan the code with Kemlock or any authenticator app. It shows up as {host}, {email}.
setup.twoStep.typeKey: Can't scan? Type this key instead:
setup.twoStep.typeCode: Type the code it shows below.
setup.twoStep.keepApp: Keep the app on a device that works without this server, such as your phone, so one outage can't lock you out of both.
setup.server.title: Server basics
setup.server.lede: The few things to choose before anyone else joins. All of it can change later in Server settings.
setup.server.notStored: Who can join, the email server, push and backups are saved by the server when you finish, and you can change them later in the admin Settings; a value the server's environment sets stays as the environment has it. The address and the files folder are configuration, not settings: changing them while the server runs would break sign-in and lose the data, so they stay in the server's environment (DOMAIN and DATA_FOLDER). What you choose here is listed on the next page, to copy into it.
setup.server.needsApi: Needs the settings API, which the server doesn't have yet.
setup.server.addressHint: Taken from the address you opened. Apps, invites and passkeys use it. The server uses the DOMAIN in its configuration; this choice is only recorded, and the admin Settings warn if they differ.
setup.server.port: Inside the container, Kemlock listens on port <mono>8080</mono>. Your reverse proxy serves this address over HTTPS.
setup.server.join.invite: People you invite, or who sign in with SSO
setup.server.join.inviteHint: SSO comes after setup, in Sign-in & SSO.
setup.server.join.domains: Anyone with an email at these domains
setup.server.join.anyone: Anyone who can reach this address
setup.server.mailHint: Sends invites. Without it, an invite is a link you copy and send yourself.
setup.server.pushHint: This server sends pushes itself: to iPhones with your APNs key, and to Android through UnifiedPush. The hosted relay is only a fallback for iPhones when no APNs key is set. Off unless you turn it on; a push says only "sync now", never what changed.
setup.server.files.s3Hint: AWS S3, MinIO, Backblaze B2, R2
setup.server.s3Config: The bucket and its keys are set in the server's configuration.
setup.server.backupsHint: Of the database and files, encrypted to an age recipient before they're written.
setup.server.backupRecipientHint: Only the matching age identity can open them. Keep that identity off this server.
setup.server.keyBody: Backups leave out this server's own key on purpose, and a restore needs it. Keep a copy apart from the backups and off this machine, such as on an offline drive.
setup.server.keyPath: It's at <mono>/data/server.key</mono> in the data volume.
setup.server.keyStored: I've stored a copy of server.key apart from the backups
setup.done.title: Your server is ready
setup.done.lede: {name} is its first admin, and the setup code no longer works.
setup.done.ledeBare: Setup is finished, and the setup code no longer works.
setup.done.signsInValue: Master password, then an authenticator app
setup.done.configNote: Who can join, the email server, push and backups are saved by the server, unless its environment sets them. The address and the files folder are configuration: copy them into the server's environment as DOMAIN and DATA_FOLDER. The address you chose is recorded, and the admin Settings warn if it isn't the one in use.
setup.done.kit.title: Make a Recovery Kit
setup.done.kit.body: Nobody can reset your master password, not even you as admin. A Recovery Kit is your way back: 3 pieces, and any 2 of them open your vault. Print or save them, and keep each in a different place.
setup.done.inviteHint: Send invites, or make spaces for a team or family
signIn.title: Sign in
signIn.lede: One account for the web vault, Kemlock, Amethystora Vault and Bitwarden apps.
signIn.passkeyCancelled: The passkey was not used. Try again, or use another way in.
signIn.passkeyUnavailable: This browser can not use a passkey here. Use another way in.
signIn.passkeyRejected: This passkey can't sign in to this account. If you added it as a two-step security key, sign in with your password and use the key as the second step.
deviceApproval.title: Sign in with another device
deviceApproval.lede: Open Kemlock on a device that is already signed in to {email}, go to Devices, and approve this request when its words match the ones below.
deviceApproval.phrase.hint: They are worked out in this browser from a one-time key it just made. Approve only if the other device shows exactly these five words.
deviceApproval.waiting: Waiting for the other device. This request lapses at {time}.
deviceApproval.denied: The other device refused this request.
deviceApproval.expired: This request lapsed or was already used. Start again to get a new one.
deviceApproval.failed: The approval could not be completed. Start again, or use your master password.
deviceApproval.refused: The server's answer did not match this browser's key, so nothing was opened. Start again, or use your master password.
sso.title: Signing you in
sso.codeNote: Your provider did not ask for a second step, so Kemlock asks for the code from your authenticator app.
sso.keyNote: Your provider did not ask for a second step, so Kemlock asks for your security key. Press the button, then touch the key when your browser asks.
sso.eitherNote: Your provider did not ask for a second step, so Kemlock asks for one: use your security key, or type the code from your authenticator app.
sso.refused: Your provider did not sign you in.
sso.lost: This sign-in was not started in this browser, or it took too long. Start again.
signIn.footer: Your master password unlocks your vault in this browser. The server never receives it.
legal.notAffiliated: Not affiliated with Bitwarden Inc. or Vaultwarden. Bitwarden is a trademark of Bitwarden Inc.
password.title: Master password
password.note: The password never leaves this browser. It unlocks your account key here; the server only checks a proof derived from it.
password.codeNote: Your account asks for a second step. Open your authenticator app and type the code it shows for this server.
password.keyNote: Your account asks for a security key as its second step. Press the button, then touch the key or approve the passkey when your browser asks.
password.eitherNote: Your account asks for a second step. Use your security key, or type the code your authenticator app shows for this server.
password.keyRejected: That security key wasn't accepted. Try again with the key you added to this account.
unlock.title: Open your vault
unlock.lede: You're signed in as {email}. This browser still needs your vault key, and only your master password makes it.
unlock.approveHint: Match a phrase, then approve on a device that is signed in
unlock.kitHint: Scan or type 2 of your 3 pieces.
unlock.kit.title: Open with your Recovery Kit
unlock.kit.lede: Enter any 2 of your 3 pieces, typed or scanned. They are checked here, in this browser, and never sent anywhere.
unlock.kit.scanning: Point the camera at the piece's QR code
unlock.kit.format: That is not a Recovery Kit piece. It starts with BMCKIT1.
unlock.kit.checksum: This piece has a typo: its check does not match. Compare it with the page, character by character.
unlock.kit.otherKit: These two pieces are from different kits.
unlock.kit.duplicate: These are the same piece twice. Use two different pieces.
unlock.kit.noKit: This account has no Recovery Kit on this server.
unlock.kit.stale: This account's kit is for an older key and opens nothing. Use the master password.
unlock.kit.wrong: These pieces do not open this account's kit. They may be from an older kit that was replaced.
table.name: Name
main.lede: Every item syncs to this server, encrypted on your devices first. The server keeps ciphertext only and can't open any of it.
main.encrypted: End-to-end encrypted · ML-KEM-1024 with X25519, then AES-256-GCM
main.empty.title: Nothing here yet
main.empty.body: Add your first login or note. It is encrypted in this browser before it is saved.
main.noMatch.title: No matches
main.noMatch.body: Nothing in this view fits. Try another word, or clear the search.
main.details.unreadable: Can't be opened in this app
item.inTrash: This item is in the Trash. Restore it to see it with your other items again.
item.unreadable: This app can't read this item. It may come from a newer app, or be sealed to a key this browser doesn't have. It is untouched on the server.
item.missing.title: Item not found
item.missing.body: It may have been deleted, or it isn't synced to this browser yet.
item.enc.title: End-to-end encrypted
item.enc.body: Encrypted on the device that saved it, then synced whole to every app signed in to your account. Each item has its own AES-256-GCM key, sealed to your account key.
item.server.title: What the server holds
item.server.note: Ciphertext, its kind, sizes and revision. No name, address, password or note.
newItem.where.in: In the space collection {collection}. Its members with access can read it.
newItem.where.inSpace: In a space. Its members with access can read it.
newItem.lede: Encrypted in this browser before it's saved. Edit opens this same form, filled in.
newItem.cantEdit: This web vault can only edit some kinds of item for now.
newItem.name: Name
newItem.generator.title: Password generator
newItem.generator.note: Made in this browser from its secure random source.
trash.title: Trash
trash.lede: Deleted items wait here for 30 days on every app, still encrypted, then go for good.
trash.none.title: The Trash is empty
trash.none.body: Items you delete wait here for 30 days before they go for good.
trash.confirmEmpty.title: Empty the Trash?
trash.confirmEmpty.body: {count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}} will be deleted for good, on every app. This can't be undone.
trash.confirmOne.title: Delete this item for good?
trash.confirmOne.body: It is deleted on every app and can't be restored.
space.collections.deleteBody: The collection is deleted for everyone in the space. This can't be undone.
space.groups.deleteBody: The group is deleted for everyone in the space. This can't be undone.
devices.title: Devices & apps
devices.lede: The apps and browsers signed in to your account, and requests to sign in.
security.title: Account security
security.lede: Two-step login, your Recovery Kit, emergency access and your keys.
placeholder.title: Not here yet
placeholder.body: This screen is waiting for the server's {needs} API. Nothing is lost: it will fill in once that API exists.
admin.overview.noAccess: Admins manage accounts. No one here can open a vault.
admin.check.secureNo: Not HTTPS: keys and passkeys won't work
admin.attention.title: Users to look at
admin.users.lede: Manage accounts and spaces. What's inside them stays out of reach.
admin.events.lede: What happened and who did it. An event names an item by its id, never by what it holds.
admin.settings.lede: The same settings Vaultwarden reads from its environment, kept in the database and changed here.
admin.settings.mail: Email: SMTP server, port, security, sender
admin.settings.storage: Storage: files, largest file, quota per user
admin.settings.backups: Backups: schedule, how many to keep, age recipient
